resources.string: %1$s. Thanks to the authors of these projects.
Enter a Google Play code to unlock Pro
Your photos stay on your own phone and in your own cloud.
The free version allows one Google and one Microsoft account. Unlock Pro to add more.
The open-source edition can sign in to one cloud account
The list of models is not available right now. Connect to the internet and try again.
More accurate models are larger and take longer to sort photos. After switching, photos are sorted again. The old model keeps working until the new one is downloaded, then it is removed.
The model and photo index will be removed to free up storage. You can download it again here or in Discover.
One in each kind of cloud
New photos are uploaded in the background right away at full quality. Identical photos are stored once.
Battery optimization delays or interrupts background backup. Once allowed, Zyll only runs briefly when there are new photos and uses no power otherwise. Tap here to set it up.
Let Zyll run in the background without battery limits
Unlock it with your original password or recovery key to see the photos you backed up before; new photos will keep being backed up. Tap here to unlock.
Earlier settings found for this account
You set up which albums to back up, Wi‑Fi only, archive, shortcuts and more on another phone before. Restore those settings?
One copy in each: Google Drive and OneDrive
Safer. Each kind of cloud gets one copy, in the highest account on the list that has space
Albums without their own setting follow the backup mode above. Albums assigned to a cloud are stored only there, even when it is full.
Backups are kept in a space reserved for Zyll in your cloud, separate from your other files, so they cannot be deleted by mistake.\u0020
They currently use about %1$s, which counts toward your cloud storage.\u0020
You can see the usage on the Google Drive website under Settings → Manage apps → Zyll Photo.
Videos are usually large and use more cloud storage
Backups won\'t use mobile data. Viewing and downloading cloud photos still can.
Your cloud needs to be reconnected. Backup is paused.
This version does not support %1$s yet
Over the free account limit. Backup is paused until you unlock Pro.
The open-source edition can use only one cloud account, so backup to this one is paused. Sign out of one account to resume.
This cloud photo cannot be found

While encryption is on, AI sorting results (used for search and sensitive content blurring) are also stored encrypted in your cloud, so a new phone or reinstall can reuse them. They are deleted when encryption is turned off.

The encrypted backup in this cloud account uses a different key from the one on this phone. Backup to this account is paused; your other accounts keep backing up. Unlock it with that backup\'s password or recovery key to see those photos, then choose which key to keep. If you no longer have them, you can abandon that old encrypted backup.
This cloud has a different encrypted backup
Connect a cloud account to continue.
You set an encryption password before. Enter the original password.
Enter the encryption password you set before.
Enter the recovery key you wrote down when turning on encryption.
Forgot both the password and the recovery key? Start over without restoring
Photos in the earlier encrypted backup of “%1$s” can never be opened once this phone deletes the key. If you might sign in to this account again, do not choose this yet.
• Photos are encrypted with AES‑256 on your phone before upload. Nobody but you can see them.
• When turned on, every photo already backed up is processed again: fetched, encrypted on this phone, then replaced in the cloud. Turning it off does the reverse. Nothing is ever left half encrypted.
• Photos still on the phone use the local original; only photos deleted from this phone are downloaded from the cloud.
• On a new phone or after reinstalling, you need the password or the recovery key. If both are lost, the encrypted backup can never be opened.
At least 10 characters, with both letters and numbers; common passwords are not allowed. You need it to restore backups on a new phone, so keep it safe.
%1$s old files are waiting to be removed from the cloud (for example originals no longer needed after encryption). This continues automatically when online.
The encryption key saved on this phone can no longer be opened (for example after changing the screen lock). Enter your encryption password or recovery key to fix it. Backup is paused until then.

This cloud has a backup you encrypted before. Unlock it with your original encryption password or recovery key to see and restore those photos, and new photos will keep being encrypted. Uploads are paused until then so that the old backup and new uploads do not use different keys.
Photos in the earlier encrypted backup will stay locked: this phone cannot show or restore them.\u0020
Turning encryption on here again will use a new key, and the old encrypted backup can never be opened.\n\n
If you might still find the original password or recovery key, do not choose this yet.
Skip restoring the earlier encrypted backup?
Off · %1$s backups waiting to be decrypted
On · %1$s older backups waiting to be encrypted
Off: photos are stored in your cloud as the original files
On: your cloud only stores ciphertext that only your password can open
Enter your encryption password to confirm. All encrypted backups in your cloud will then be converted back to normal files.
Unlock the earlier encrypted backup above first.
These accounts still have an earlier encrypted backup: %1$s. Encryption is fully turned off only after you reconnect them and they are processed. Until then the key stays on this phone.
Processing continues when the network allows (for example on Wi‑Fi). No new photos are uploaded meanwhile, so nothing ends up half encrypted.

If you forget the password, this key also unlocks your backup. After you check \"I have saved it\" and tap Done, Zyll no longer keeps it. If you lose it, you can get a new one with your password in End-to-end encryption.
%1$s photos and videos that are fully backed up to your cloud will be deleted from this phone. They still show in the gallery (with a cloud mark)
, open with a tap and can be restored to the phone at any time. Photos that are not fully backed up are never deleted.
Space freed. The photos are still in your cloud storage.
How many days after a screenshot is taken should it be archived? Archived screenshots leave the timeline but stay in Albums → Archive. Screenshots you unarchive are not archived again.
Nudity and explicit content are blurred until you tap “Show anyway”, so browsing in public is never awkward.
%1$s sensitive photos detected. Everything runs on this phone; photos are never uploaded.
Sorting photos %1$s/%2$s. Sorted photos are checked right away. %3$s detected so far.
This needs the on-device AI model (shared with smart search). Download it first, then you can turn this on.
• Detection uses the on-device Chinese-CLIP model. Everything runs on your phone; photos are never uploaded.
• Detection is never 100% accurate: swimwear or baby photos may be flagged, and some photos may be missed. Blurred photos can always be opened.
• In the photo viewer you can also choose “Don\'t blur for 10 minutes” or turn it off.
Photos only in the cloud are not checked and may show unblurred. Turn this on to download and check their thumbnails.
Photos backed up and deleted from this phone have their thumbnails downloaded and checked. Unchecked ones stay blurred so downloaded thumbnails are never exposed.
Pro feature: search photos by text and sort them automatically
%1$s albums are excluded. You can turn them on in each album.
Every album on this phone is backed up
Google Drive / OneDrive. Back up to both, or choose per album.
%1$s items backed up, %2$s can be freed
Photos already in your cloud can be removed from this phone and still show in the gallery
Off: every delete must be confirmed in a system dialog
On: deleting and favoriting no longer ask for confirmation
Albums that appear later (for example from a newly installed app) are backed up too
Screenshots move to Archive after %1$s days and leave the timeline
Off. AI detects nudity and similar content and blurs it first.
On, waiting for the AI model to download

Unlocked: %1$s. Its photos can be viewed now. To keep things simple, all your backups will use one key. The photos encrypted with the other key will be re-encrypted in the background (following your backup network settings). Until you choose, backup to this account stays paused.
Keep the key on this phone
Keep the key I just unlocked
Keep using the password and recovery key you set on this phone. Photos in the account you just unlocked will be re-encrypted with it, and the old key will then be deleted from this phone.

From now on, use the password and recovery key of the backup you just unlocked. Everything encrypted with this phone\'s current key will be re-encrypted with it. This phone\'s current encryption password and the recovery key shown when you set up encryption here will both stop working. Other phones still using the current key will need to unlock again with the previous backup\'s password. This can\'t be undone.
Used in this order: No. 1 is preferred, and the next one is used when it is full. A photo is stored at most once in Google Drive and once in OneDrive.
Photos already backed up stay in that cloud, but Zyll will stop backing up to it and won\'t show them here. Sign in again any time to get them back.
Stored in the first account with space: %1$s
You unlocked a backup that uses a different key. Choose which key to keep; that account is paused until then. Tap here.
Up to 4 accounts per kind of cloud. Backup to this account is paused; disconnect another one to continue.
Only one kind of cloud is connected, so only one copy is kept for now. Connect %1$s to keep a second copy.
At least 10 characters, letters and numbers
Sensitive content protection will also stop working: new photos won\'t be checked and photos already found won\'t be blurred.
Detecting sensitive photos uses the on-device AI model, which is part of Pro.
Downloading the AI model. You can turn this on once it finishes.
Photos not checked yet are not blurred until they are checked.
Download the AI model to use this
Another phone turned on encryption for %1$s, but it is off on this phone. Until you choose, this phone won\'t convert those backups.
Another phone turned off encryption for %1$s, but it is on on this phone. Until you choose, this phone won\'t convert those backups.
Damaged backups in your cloud drive that can\'t be opened: %1$d. Photos still on this phone will be backed up again.
The backup list in %1$s is damaged. Backups to this account are paused.
Rebuild it from this phone: the damaged copy is kept as a separate file, then a new list is written.
The backup list in %1$s is older than the one this phone saw last time (the drive may have been restored). Backups to this account are paused.
\n\nPhotos only in this account (not on this phone or in other accounts): %1$d. They will disappear from the gallery until you connect again.
This is your last cloud account. If you sign in again later, Zyll keeps backing up with your current settings.
Also reset backup settings to defaults (auto backup, Wi‑Fi only, videos, album choices, etc.)
Also remove the encryption key from this phone (encrypted backups in the cloud stay; after signing in again you\'ll need your password or recovery key)

Once removed, if you forget your password and don\'t have the recovery key, the encrypted photos in the cloud can never be opened. Shared albums and links on this phone are cleared too and come back after you sign in and unlock. Auto backup is turned off. While disconnected, Zyll can\'t see changes made in that cloud by other devices.
Photos already in this account can still be viewed and restored.
The system picker caches thumbnails, so you may need to reopen the picker for the change to show.
Turned on, but it won\'t take effect until the on-device AI model is ready.
Rebuilding… this can take a few seconds.
The rebuild didn\'t finish (possibly a network problem). Try again later.
Use this phone\'s list: this phone\'s records replace the older backup list in the drive. Photos you already deleted won\'t come back.
Use the drive\'s list: sync again from the older backup list in the drive. Photos deleted after that point may show up again, and recent backups are checked again.
The older backup list in %1$s will be used. Photos deleted after it was saved may reappear in the gallery. If you\'re not sure why the drive was restored, choose \"Use this phone\'s list\" instead.
Both the password and the recovery key unlock your encrypted backup. If you forget one, use the other to set it again. Photos are not uploaded or encrypted again.

Enter your current password. After this the old recovery key stops working, so write down the new one. Your other devices follow the next time they go online (update any that are on an old version first).

First confirm it is you with your current password or the recovery key, then set a new password. After this the old password stops working. Your other devices follow the next time they go online (update any that are on an old version first).
Forgot the password? Use the recovery key
Password changed. Use the new password on new phones and on the web.
The password or recovery key was changed on another device, and this phone has switched to the new one. Use the new password and recovery key from now on; the old ones no longer work.
Delete every Zyll backup in your cloud accounts and start over. Photos currently on this phone are not affected.
This deletes %1$d Zyll files (%2$s in total) from %4$s, including %3$d photos and videos.
No photos have been backed up yet. Resetting deletes the %1$d files Zyll left in %2$s and clears the encryption key on this phone, so you start over.
Deleted data can never be recovered. Zyll has no way to bring it back.
• The encryption key is deleted too, so the current password and recovery key stop working.
• Albums you shared stop working. Albums others shared with you need to be joined again from the link.

• Automatic backup is turned off. Other phones and the web version stop backing up to these accounts on their own once updated to the new version; disconnect any that are still on an old version first, or they will upload the photos again.
• OneDrive first moves deleted files to its recycle bin. To remove them completely, empty the recycle bin on the OneDrive website.
• Photos on this phone are not deleted.
I know what I am doing
You can leave this page. Deleting continues in the background.
All backup data was deleted. Turn automatic backup back on to start over; to encrypt again you need to set a new password, as the old one no longer works.
Deleting all backup data stopped partway, so backup is paused. Tap Continue to delete the rest.
%1$d of these photos and videos are no longer on this phone (for example, ones removed with Free up space). Once deleted they are gone for good.
• Photos currently on this phone are not deleted.
The password was changed on another device, and this phone has switched over. Use the new password from now on; the old one no longer works. The recovery key is unchanged.
The recovery key was replaced on another device, and this phone has switched over. The old recovery key no longer works; use the new one you wrote down on that device. The password is unchanged.

The new password or recovery key has not reached %1$s yet. Until it does, the old password and recovery key still apply there and the new ones do not work yet. It will be sent automatically once you are online.
Changed on this phone, but some cloud accounts have not received it yet. It will be sent automatically once you are online. See End-to-end encryption for details.
All backups in %1$s were deleted on another device, so this phone has paused backing up to these accounts. To start over from this phone, tap the button below.
Start backing up again from this phone
%1$d files could not be deleted due to permissions and remain in the cloud.

All Zyll backups in %1$s were deleted on another device. This phone has stopped backing up to these accounts and cleared its backup records for them. The photos on your phone are not affected. You can start again from Backup when you want.
• Photos you added to other people\'s shared albums are not deleted; ask them to remove them if needed.
This phone will treat %1$s as empty accounts and back up from the start: all photos selected for backup will be uploaded again, which can take a long time and use a lot of data. Continue?
